content:
Apple released updated Mac mini and Mac Studio models on the quiet just days before its September event, surprising many. These announcements were generally expected to be part of the event itself.

One strong argument is that the company probably had a lot of significant news to get through in its "Awe dropping" keynote, and wanted to get these updates out of the way. But a new report offers an alternative explanation…

The fact that new Mac mini and Mac Studio models were announced just two weeks before the September 9 event came as a surprise. Why not wait those two weeks and unveil them properly as part of the event, rather than just a press release?

The Information reports that the decision was made because Apple was taken aback by the level of demand for these models for AI applications, and certain configurations have been out of stock for months, so Apple decided to get the news out early.

9to5Mac Opinion

There's no doubt that the power of Apple Silicon has made the Mac mini and Mac Studio popular choices for those who want to run AI models locally. We've seen, for example, researchers using Thunderbolt 5 to combine four Mac Studios into a powerful AI cluster.

I also believe that Apple didn't originally anticipate demand on this scale.

However, it's harder to buy that two weeks would make any meaningful difference to the situation. That gap is too small for me to find it a credible explanation. Personally, I think the argument we made earlier is the more likely one.

Apple wants to heavily promote the launch of its first foldable iPhone, and ensure the iPhone 18 Pro doesn't look like a sideshow. If Apple unveils the HomePad smart home hub as expected, that will also be a major announcement.

Throw in a new Apple TV and HomePod mini 2 — both with Siri AI — two new Apple Watch models, and possibly new AirPods. That's a lot to fit into a single keynote, and I can completely understand Apple wanting to get these Mac desktops out of the way early.

What do you think? Please share your thoughts in the comments.
